I farm in Quzhou County, so I will stay with the wheat-maize rotation that fits my land, my labor, and the local weather best. I know this system, I can manage it without taking big market or technical risks, and it gives me grain in both parts of the year. I will keep winter wheat on the land through the first half of the year, then I will follow it with summer maize after harvest. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want steadier emergence, better yield, and less risk than keeping older seed. For wheat, I will fertilize enough to support tillering and grain filling, irrigate several times because spring here can turn dry, and spray only when disease or insects are likely to cut yield. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into maize, keep tillage lighter to save time and moisture, feed the crop mainly with nitrogen, and irrigate when the summer rain is not enough. I am choosing a simple, familiar plan because it is the safest way for me to protect output and manage the whole year with confidence.
